title: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 5
summary: From artificial intelligence to migration, some of the forces reshaping the twenty-first century took centre stage at the UN General Assembly on Saturday. Leaders wrestled with a common dilemma: how to harness profound technological and social change without allowing it to deepen the divisions already separating countries and communities. This edition of The Takeaway distils key points from Day 5 of the annual high-level debate.

title: Canada urges stronger partnerships as global order faces ‘rupture’
summary: Canada’s Foreign Minister Anita Anand warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that the international order has entered an era of profound disruption, calling for stronger multilateral cooperation and new partnerships as major powers increasingly turn away from global economic integration.

title: Countries far from conflict paying the price for wars not their own, India tells UN
summary: India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar warned on Saturday that violent conflicts continue to undermine international peace and security, while countries far removed from the battlefield are being forced to pay a heavy price.

title: Saudi Arabia warns Gulf security inseparable from global stability amid regional tensions

title: Lavrov issues call for new Eurasian ‘security architecture’

title: ‘Safeguard the postwar order,’ China tells UN General Assembly

title: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 4
summary: From the Caribbean to the Pacific, leaders from small island States demanded climate justice, ocean protection and greater solidarity at the UN General Assembly on Friday.  They warned that rising seas are already redrawing national boundaries, while the ripple effects of faraway wars are being felt on their shores. This edition of The Takeaway summarizes key points made during the fourth day of the annual high-level debate.

title: Haiti at ‘watershed moment’, Prime Minister tells UN, urging full backing for security force
summary: Haiti is at a “watershed moment” in its struggle against gang violence and needs sustained international support alongside stronger national security institutions, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé told the UN General Assembly on Friday.

title: Tuvalu urges decisive global action as rising seas threaten its future

title: LIVE: Six years on from COVID-19, is the world ready for the next pandemic?

World leaders are meeting Friday to review the lessons learned and cement a new approach to prevention and preparation for the next pandemic. Hopes are high that a World Health Organization-led international agreement can move forward.

title: Haitians can’t wait to return home and vote in elections says Prime Minister

A people who can wait no longer.  A people waiting to regain security, to return home to work, to send their children to school, and to freely choose their leaders.” Those are the words of the Haitian Prime Minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, who spoke at a special UN meeting on the future of security in Haiti.
